summary: Calling out is frequent, polite and fast but lopsided: GPT-5.4 sends 98 of 324 challenge messages, and the 29 of 57 verified incidents that were raised were raised in a median 2.4 min, conceded in a median 0.9 min. But 26 incidents were never raised, private notice followed by silence shows up for only 2 of them, and no agent took a concern about a peer to humans.

questions.question: Who challenges whose work, and how often? A challenge expression ("how were these produced", "doesn't match", "could not reproduce", "please verify", "correction", and others you find), validated on a sample; resolve short names to agents. Speaker x target counts; top caller-outer.
questions.answer: 324 goal-41 chat messages challenge another agent's work, 256 with a resolvable target; GPT-5.4 is the top caller-out (98 messages, 30%), mostly at Claude Opus 4.5 (22), Claude Haiku 4.5 and DeepSeek-V3.2 (15 each), and in #best Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 each target Gemini 3.1 Pro 12 times. Gemini 2.5 Pro, Kimi K2.6 and GPT-5 are challenged (25, 21, 1) but almost never challenge (4, 1, 1 messages, none at a named agent).
questions.precision: expression: 14 of 25 (seed 41), counts not reported; stored callout label: 21 of 25 are challenges, 15 of 18 resolved targets right (seed 41)
questions.limits: Counts rest on the stored 'callout' label (calls_out_other); 68 challenges name no agent and are left out of the matrix.

questions.question: For each verified incident, who caught it, and how many minutes after it became visible to the room? Take the incidents from s1_rest_study.json, s2_best_study.json, s3_claims.json, q1a_graders.json, q1b_c1_c3.json (deduplicate), and match each to the first challenge message by program; verify each match.
questions.answer: Of 57 deduplicated incidents, 29 were raised by someone else (23 direct challenges, 6 corrective fixes), 2 were first admitted by the culprit and 26 never; the median delay was 2.4 min (20 of 29 within 7 min), the longest 2,792 min. Catchers: GPT-5.4 10, Claude Opus 4.7 6, GPT-5.5 5, GPT-5.2 4, Claude Haiku 4.5 2, Claude Opus 4.5 2.

questions.question: Which agents reported their own errors before anyone else found them? Self-correction phrases with no earlier challenge by others; per-agent count.
questions.answer: 13 unprompted self-corrections by 9 agents: GPT-5.4 4, GPT-5.2 2, one each for Claude Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.5, DeepSeek-V3.2 and Gemini 3.1 Pro. 9 more admissions came only after a challenge, including all 3 of Gemini 2.5 Pro's.
questions.precision: 24 matches, all read: 21 are own-error reports; the program's no-earlier-challenge test agreed with the hand reading on 13 of 24, hand flags used
questions.limits: First-person error words are rare, so recall is low (a fix announced as "Fixed syntax error" is missed; one such case added from W2).

questions.question: How did the challenged agent respond: concede, defend or ignore, and how fast? Per-agent concede rate and median minutes.
questions.answer: Over the 29 verified catches (31 culprit responses), 18 conceded, 1 fixed silently, 3 defended, 1 answered about something else and 8 ignored; concessions came in a median 0.9 min (max 14.5). Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2 conceded every time, Gemini 3.1 Pro 5 of 8, Claude Haiku 4.5 only 2 of 7.
questions.precision: automatic classifier over all W1 challenges 9 of 25 (seed 41), not reported; all 31 responses read by hand
questions.limits: Only verified incidents; a reply after 3 hours counts as ignore.

questions.question: Do call-outs go to the agents who assign tasks, or only to those who receive them? Join W1 with the stored `delegation` labels (label `directs`); yes or no with counts.
questions.answer: Yes: the five agents who direct most (DeepSeek-V3.2, Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Opus 4.7) receive 133 of 299 call-out links. But in one-way pairs (A directs B, never the reverse) call-outs go down 77 times and up 24.
questions.precision: 'directs' label 21 of 25 are assignments (seed 41); call-out label as W1
questions.limits: Task links here count every room-mate named in an assigning message, so they run higher than the addressee-only counts in Leadership L1 (for example DeepSeek-V3.2: 65 links here, 19 messages and 38 real task links there). Assignees = all room-mates named in a directs message, so a few merely mentioned agents count as assignees.
